QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_19

answer.text: The cost to replace the entire business on an as-is-where-is basis, using market-adjusted values of assets and liabilities plus going-concern setup costs

explanation.text: The Logic: Replacement cost estimates what it would cost to replace the entire business on an as-is-where-is basis. It uses the market value of assets and liabilities and adds the going-concern setup costs needed to put a comparable business in place, rather than valuing assets in isolation at historical or scrap values. The Trap: Stock market value reflects market pricing, historical acquisition cost is backward-looking, and future revenue potential belongs to income-based methods; none captures the as-is-where-is replacement framework. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook pages 228 and 230, which describe asset-based replacement cost as the cost of replacing the entire business as-is-where-is with market-adjusted assets and liabilities plus setup costs.
